source.basis: Operator spec page; structured facts only, no operator prose reproduced.

reading.body:
CyrusOne Lewisville DFW2 publishes 12 MW of IT capacity across 200,000 square feet of technical space, making it too small for large-scale AI training clusters which typically require 50+ MW per campus.

At general-purpose colocation densities of 40 kW per rack, this power budget could support roughly 300 racks. At higher densities typical of AI training, such as 150 kW per rack, the same 12 MW would support approximately 80 racks of accelerator infrastructure. The facility's power envelope limits it to small to mid-sized deployments rather than the concentrated compute clusters AI training demands.

The facility holds certifications for PCI DSS, HIPAA, ISO 27001, FISMA, SSAE 16 Type II, and TIA-942 tier classification. These enable it to host regulated workloads in healthcare, finance, and government. These certifications do not indicate AI-specific infrastructure or readiness for accelerator-heavy workloads.

Lewisville DFW2 represents 2.5 percent of Texas's published 475 MW of data center IT capacity. Texas has 133 mapped data center sites but only nineteen publish power figures. This data gap means the actual scale of available power in the state is unknown, and comparisons between facilities rely on a sparse subset of disclosed capacity.
